headline_marked: Hackers claim [[19 million Pathao users' data leaked]] and demand $400,000
headline: Hackers claim 19 million Pathao users' data leaked and demand $400,000
summary: The company admits some personal information was accessed by attackers, while hackers claim to have stolen NID, driving license, and bank details.
details: A hacker group claims to have stolen data from approximately 19 million Pathao users, demanding $400,000 to prevent the release of the information.
The stolen data allegedly includes phone numbers, emails, National ID (NID) numbers, driving licenses, locations, Facebook profiles, and home addresses.
Pathao confirmed in a statement that 'some personal information,' including names, email addresses, and phone numbers, was accessed by attackers.
The company stated that they took critical systems offline as a precautionary measure on October 4 after detecting a cyber-security incident, which caused temporary service disruptions.
The hackers claim to possess 133 GB of data comprising 250 million records across 591 databases, with the largest database containing over 19 million accounts.
Beyond user data, the group claims to have accessed internal business information, including employee records, administrative access logs, and merchant bank account details.
Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha has urged Pathao to conduct an independent digital forensic investigation and preserve all digital evidence for law enforcement.
Pathao has engaged external cyber security experts to secure its systems and says it will update relevant authorities once the full investigation is completed.
caption:
19 million users' data potentially leaked. Hackers are demanding $400,000 to keep it secret.

A hacker group claims to have stolen data from approximately 19 million Pathao users, demanding $400,000 to prevent the release of the information.

The stolen data allegedly includes phone numbers, emails, National ID (NID) numbers, driving licenses, locations, Facebook profiles, and home addresses.

Pathao confirmed in a statement that 'some personal information,' including names, email addresses, and phone numbers, was accessed by attackers.

The company stated that they took critical systems offline as a precautionary measure on October 4 after detecting a cyber-security incident, which caused temporary service disruptions.

The hackers claim to possess 133 GB of data comprising 250 million records across 591 databases, with the largest database containing over 19 million accounts.

Beyond user data, the group claims to have accessed internal business information, including employee records, administrative access logs, and merchant bank account details.

Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha has urged Pathao to conduct an independent digital forensic investigation and preserve all digital evidence for law enforcement.

Pathao has engaged external cyber security experts to secure its systems and says it will update relevant authorities once the full investigation is completed.

headline_marked: Trump says [[US will not attack Iran]] before November midterms
headline: Trump says US will not attack Iran before November midterms
summary: President Donald Trump claims 'productive' talks are underway to end the six-month-old war, though Tehran refuses to abandon uranium enrichment.
details: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that the US will not launch an attack on Iran before the midterm congressional elections on November 3rd.
Trump described current discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran as 'productive,' asserting that both nations are working toward ending the conflict.
The war began in February after US and Israeli strikes on Iran, and has since contributed to a decline in Trump's domestic approval ratings.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll shows approximately 60 percent of Americans, including one in four Republicans, disapprove of Trump's handling of the Iran situation.
The conflict has caused gasoline prices to spike, increasing pressure on voters who are primarily concerned with the cost of living.
While Trump expects oil prices to drop after the elections, he has not yet provided a detailed plan for exiting the war.
Recent proposals to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz have been exchanged, though Trump has rejected Tehran's latest offer.
Iran's state media reported that Tehran will not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium stockpile, despite US demands for 'meaningful' reductions.
caption:
No attacks on Iran before November 3rd. Trump says talks are 'productive' as midterm elections approach.

President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that the US will not launch an attack on Iran before the midterm congressional elections on November 3rd.

Trump described current discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran as 'productive,' asserting that both nations are working toward ending the conflict.

The war began in February after US and Israeli strikes on Iran, and has since contributed to a decline in Trump's domestic approval ratings.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll shows approximately 60 percent of Americans, including one in four Republicans, disapprove of Trump's handling of the Iran situation.

The conflict has caused gasoline prices to spike, increasing pressure on voters who are primarily concerned with the cost of living.

While Trump expects oil prices to drop after the elections, he has not yet provided a detailed plan for exiting the war.

Recent proposals to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz have been exchanged, though Trump has rejected Tehran's latest offer.

Iran's state media reported that Tehran will not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium stockpile, despite US demands for 'meaningful' reductions.
